free_tier.stated: Compute, model and platform allocations from federal agencies and contributing partners, 'awarded for twelve (12) months duration', spread across a resource catalogue that includes national-lab and commercial partner capacity. The eligibility sentence and the email rule are the whole finding: 'This call is open to meritorious proposals by US-based researchers and educators from US-based institutions including academic institutions ..., non-profits, federal agencies or federally funded R&D centers, state, local, or tribal agencies, startups and small businesses with federal grants.' and 'Note that the email address you provide must be your institutional email. Requests providing personal email addresses such as .gmail.com addresses will not be considered.'

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: None. The allocation is bound to a US institution and to a named PI whose affiliation is published, so it cannot be held by an individual.

limits.value: a US institutional email is checked before the proposal is read, and the proposal itself needs a three-page PDF plus a peer review, so an unaffiliated applicant is excluded twice.

NSF established a NAIRR Operations Center on 1 September 2026 led by the San Diego Supercomputer Center, so the programme is transitioning rather than closing

notes: Worth recording because NAIRR is the program a reader is most likely to be told to try, and the exclusion is unusually explicit: not only an institution, but an institutional email address, with the .gmail case named. The one softening clause is real and should not be overstated - 'Proposals for research activities without merit-reviewed support will be accepted' removes the federal-grant precondition inside the eligible institution class, but does not create an unaffiliated lane. The pilot's own end date is unbounded ('until the end of the NAIRR Pilot program or until all resources have been committed'), which is a second reason not to treat it as durable capacity.
